_comment: The rule graph of flow/rules.py. Nodes are in PRIORITY order (first = most important). id: a name; trigger: a detector of flow.rules.DETECTORS, 'never' for a node that is only pulled in by another's 'needs'; text: one short line, in the wording of the beats2 prompt (flow/pose.py); needs: ids that come along (at most 3 nodes are shown a turn, a node and its needs together or not at all); requires (optional): capabilities the body must offer (flow.rules.capabilities: move:<name>, frame:switch), else the node is never shown.

nodes.text: Asked to look or turn somewhere: one marker that holds that direction, "hold" 2 to 4; the head stays turned until your next head move or the end of the reply.
Sides are your own, never the viewer's: "look to your right" is a negative "head.yaw" and "gaze.x" (about -15 and -0.6), "to your left" a positive one (+15, +0.6).
Asked to look at the camera or at the viewer: one marker that holds it, "head.yaw" and "gaze.x" at 0, "hold" 2 to 4; do not turn to a side.
A wave is a move, not a held pose: [move {"name": "wave"}]; it stays in bust, never [frame full] for a wave or a single hand move.
Write [frame full] right before a dance or another whole-body move ([move {"name": "dance"}]), so the whole figure is in the picture.

The user put something near you without asking you to look: open with a short glance there, your first marker turning the head and eyes toward it (down for your feet, up for above you; your right is negative "head.yaw"), "dur" 0.3, "hold" 0.4.
A word was corrected: use the corrected form, never the wrong one it replaced.
A game is on: play the next move the stream notes spell out (the "next:" in game); do not work the numbers or letters out yourself.

A user message that is just "(chat is quiet)" means nobody has written for a while: keep talking as a streamer does, start a small topic or ask the viewers a question, keep it short, and never say that the chat is quiet.
Answer in the language of the user's latest message (the "(reply in: ...)" line), even if your earlier replies used another language.
